notes: aids: an element is a reading aid when its type and supertype, each trimmed and folded as the room profile defines it, are one of pairs, and it carries mark.field, read by presence: any value but null, a string only when something is left after trimming White_Space. The pair without the mark is lore; the mark on no pair makes nothing.

element: isCharterElement(element), in the room profile's matcher-case shape: element gives type, supertype and the mark as a body might carry them; is_charter_element is what the reader must answer, the pair AND the mark. A mark counts when its value is not null: a string only when something is left after the White_Space trim, any other value (a number, an object) as present; the value is never compared.

worlds: each world's elements as its owner is served them, the ids its hidden mark keeps from every reader but the owner, and its readers, in the lens fixture's shape. A reader's rung is owner (the whole world), contributor (the world less the hidden), guest (exactly the whole and known_of ids it lists; known_of is a stub: a name, its description and its dates, no link and no extension field) or public (the world less the hidden and the room elements, and nothing at all unless the world carries open: true, a world open to anyone). A case's world is a name in worlds or, as a graph case's is, a world of its own.

a stub's standing: a stub serves no extension field, so whether an element the reader holds only as a stub is a reading aid is read from the element as the owner is served it; what the reading shows of it is what the stub serves.

charter: want is charterOf(world, reader). charter is {id, name, rules, skill} or null: the newest marked Charter the reader sees, by created_at compared as instants (none sorts oldest), then the higher id by code point; rules the rules_field list as stored, [] when absent or null; skill the ids its description names (any id written as 8-4-4-4-12 hex, so every ow:// form, a site address and a bare id), in lowercase, each once in the order written, kept when it is an Object of this world the reader sees (served whole to every reader who reads the Charter; a hidden one is not seen and not kept), the first skill_max of those kept. guide is {id, name} or null, chosen the same way among marked Guides. domains is every marked Domain the reader sees, each {id, name, sentence, hubs}: in the order of the Guide's constructs as the reader is served them first (an id named twice keeps its first place, an entry that is no marked Domain is skipped), then the rest by folded name and then id; with no Guide seen, by folded name and id alone.

sentence: the description as served up to its first line break (a line feed or a carriage return), trimmed of White_Space; an empty string when there is none. hubs: the distinct {type, id} the Domain's served link fields name, in hub_fields' order (the Construct's link fields, the schema's order) and each list's own order, the Domain itself excluded; a stub serves no links, so a stub Domain's hubs are [].

mark.value: the id of the world the aid was written for; read by presence, never by its value

cases.name: harbour-owner-reads-the-whole-packet
cases.note: The newest marked Charter (the unmarked, newer one is lore); its skill in text order, the hidden Object kept for the owner; the Guide's order with a doubled entry once and a lore Construct skipped; then the two Domains the Guide does not name, by folded name; each sentence cut at the first line break (a carriage return in the Docks) and trimmed; a Domain's link to itself is no hub.

cases.name: harbour-contributor-a-hidden-domain-and-hub-are-not-there
cases.note: The Vault and the Sealed Orders are hidden: the Vault is not listed and nothing marks the gap, the Orders are neither skill nor hub.

cases.name: harbour-guest-the-charter-whole-its-skill-whole-a-stub-domain-a-name
cases.note: The Charter whole to a guest (the keeper's house rules), its skill Objects served whole beside it, as to every reader who reads the Charter, and kept; the Lighthouse a stub: its name and served sentence, no hubs; a hub outside the guest's slice left out; ash row, which names the guest's own Character, is in its slice and listed after the Guide's order; Domains the guest does not see are not listed.

cases.name: a-public-reader-on-a-closed-world-reads-nothing
cases.note: The Charter is the public's only on a world open to anyone.

cases.name: two-charters-at-one-instant-the-higher-id-a-guide-with-no-created-at-the-oldest
cases.note: The two Charters were made at one instant, written in two offsets: the higher id by code point leads. The Guide with no created_at sorts oldest, under a higher id. Rules B's rules are not read, Rules A has none: [].

cases.name: the-pairs-without-the-mark-are-lore
cases.note: A Charter, a Guide and a Domain with no mark are lore; the mark on no pair, or on a word that only resembles one (Domains), makes no reading aid.

cases.name: the-mark-by-presence-trimmed-as-the-room-profile-trims
cases.note: A mark naming another world counts (presence, never its value) and the pair is trimmed and folded; a mark of a no-break space and a space is blank, so the newer Law is lore; a mark of U+001F is a mark (not White_Space); an empty mark is none.

cases.name: a-guide-the-owner-sees-orders-the-domains
cases.note: The Guide is hidden from every reader but the owner, who reads its order.

cases.name: no-guide-seen-the-domains-by-folded-name-and-id
cases.note: No Guide this reader sees: the Domains by folded name, then id (north and " North " fold alike, the lower id first); the guide is null.

cases.name: a-public-reader-on-an-open-world
cases.note: Open to anyone: the public reads the Charter, the Guide and the Domains it sees, less the hidden and the room elements (no skill, no hub, no Domain from either).

cases.name: an-open-world-read-by-its-owner
cases.note: The owner's reading of the same world: the hidden Domain after the Guide's, the hidden Object and the room line as hubs in the schema's field order.

cases.name: skill-each-id-once-in-order-objects-of-this-world-the-first-five
cases.note: Every form in one text: each id once in the order written (an uppercase id read in lowercase), kept only as an Object of this world (the world's own id, a Character and another world's Object dropped), the first five of those kept.

cases.name: skill-the-five-are-counted-after-the-cut
cases.note: The Tongs are hidden from this reader: cut first, so the sixth Object written comes in.

cases.name: skill-form-ow-object
cases.note: One form alone; a world carried by the case, as a graph case does.

cases.note: The guest knows the Guide only as a stub, a name and an id: it is still the Guide, answered as {id, name}. A stub serves no links, so its constructs order nothing: the Domains the guest sees come by folded name and id alone, ash row first, where the Guide's stored order would put the Archive and the Docks first.

cases.name: a-proposed-charter-is-no-readers-charter
cases.note: A proposed element is in no reader's view, the owner's included (any value but null: a seat's mark or a doubt): the newer Charter and Guide are proposed, so the settled ones lead; the Annex carries a doubt and is no Domain; the Draft Ledger is proposed, so it is kept neither in the skill nor in the Hall's hubs.

cases.name: a-member-reading-the-charter-as-a-stub-reads-it-whole
cases.note: The guest's slice holds the Charter only as a known-of stub, which serves no extension field: the Charter is every member rung's to read whole, so its rules and its skill come from the Charter itself, not from the stub.

cases.name: a-skill-id-compares-as-a-uuid-whatever-its-case
cases.note: An id compares as a UUID, whatever its case: the Object written in uppercase hex and again in lowercase is one Object, kept once, in lowercase.

cases.name: a-skill-id-named-only-in-uppercase-is-kept
cases.note: The only copy of the skill's id in the Charter's text is in uppercase hex: a reader that compares the text as written finds no such Object and drops it; read as a UUID it is the Object, kept, in lowercase.
